title: Rational Fibonacci–Catalan polynomials: positivity, a Coxeter classification and q-Fibonomial unimodality up to width seven
oneLine: A six-year-old positivity observation proved for every pair, an exact Coxeter table, and unimodality up to width seven
abstract: Replacing each whole number j in a binomial coefficient or Catalan number by the q-integer of the Fibonacci number F_j gives the q-Fibonomial coefficients and the rational Fibonacci–Catalan functions C_{m,n}(q) of Bergeron, Ceballos and Küstner. Following S. X. Li, C_{m,n} is a polynomial when gcd(m,n) ≤ 2; Bergeron, Ceballos and Küstner observed nonnegative coefficients in every computed case and asked what they count. This candidate proves the nonnegativity for every such pair: for every pair the reduced denominator is exactly the q-integer of F_gcd(m,n), and the reduced numerator is the Hilbert series of an Artinian weighted complete intersection. The known complete-intersection criterion is verified by a new uniform semigroup count using Fibonacci divisibility, which covers the pairs with comparable indices that existing sufficient conditions leave open. The same holds for Lucas sequences with positive coprime parameters. For the analogous product attached to any irreducible finite reflection group, the shifts that give a polynomial are determined exactly and every such polynomial is positive, including every Fuss–Catalan case. The q-Fibonomial unimodality conjecture is proved whenever the smaller index is at most seven (widths five to seven by exact computer certificates), on a set of pairs of density about 0.408, and for each fixed width once the larger index is large. Limits: no combinatorial model on the original tilings, and the full unimodality conjecture remains open. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.
citeText: Anonymous (2026). Rational Fibonacci–Catalan polynomials: positivity, a Coxeter classification and q-Fibonomial unimodality up to width seven. Version 0.1.0-candidate. Evidence Press. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24541015
evidence: A 14-page paper with a plain introduction (the objects, why they matter, what was known, what is new and a roadmap), written proofs of Theorems 3.1, 6.1, 7.1 and 8.1, Corollary 4.1 and the infinite families of Theorem 5.1, open problems and an AI-use statement. Seven standard-library Python programs in exact integer and rational arithmetic accompany it: verify_type_a.py (Theorem 3.1 on 104 pairs, the support test on 8695 subsets, Example 3.3, Corollary 4.1), two independent certificates for the exceptional reflection groups (verify_exceptional.py, verify_pairs.py), verify_classical.py (187 classical and dihedral cases), claims.py, width_cert.py (widths four to seven) and replay.py. A clean replay in Python's optimised mode reproduced all nine certificate runs; corrupting the H3 residues or the positivity check makes the programs fail; Linux CI reruns them. The exceptional rows of Theorem 5.1 and Theorem 9.1 (widths five to seven) depend on the programs; elsewhere they are cross-checks.

keyResults: Theorem 3.1 (proof): for every pair (m,n) the reduced denominator of C_{m,n} is [F_gcd(m,n)]_q and the rest is the Hilbert series of an Artinian weighted complete intersection; hence C_{m,n} has nonnegative coefficients exactly when gcd(m,n) ≤ 2. Example: C_{10,4} = [89]_q([72]_{q²}[77]_{q³} + q²³¹[48]_{q³}).
Corollary 4.1 (proof): the same denominator and complete-intersection structure for Lucas sequences with coprime positive parameters, such as the Pell numbers.

Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.2: for every irreducible finite reflection group the shifts giving a polynomial are listed exactly and all such polynomials are positive (proofs for types A, B, D and I₂(k); exceptional types by two independent exact certificates); every Fuss–Catalan case is positive; for B₃ with shift 3 the product is [21]_q, correcting a stated condition for types B and D.
Theorems 6.1 and 7.1 (proof): P_{m,n} is unimodal on a set of pairs of density about 0.408, and for each fixed n ≥ 4 increases strictly to the centre once m is large.
Theorems 8.1 and 9.1: P_{m,n} is unimodal whenever min(m,n) ≤ 7 (previously three); width four by proof, widths five to seven by exact certificates.

Limits and credit: no combinatorial model on the original tilings, so the 2020 open problem stays open in its intended sense; the full unimodality conjecture is open; twisted and reducible cases are not treated. Polynomiality is due to S. X. Li; unimodality implies positivity to Aliniaeifard and Connelly et al.; the complete-intersection criterion and the widely separated case to Gatzweiler, Levicán-Santibáñez and Yoshida.
